Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) shows a small, hypoplastic right lung with opacity and ipsilateral mediastinal/heart shift (dextroposition), while the CT images highlight an anomalous venous drainage (Scimitar sign). These findings are classic for Scimitar syndrome (hypogenetic lung syndrome), which involves right lung aplasia/hypoplasia and partial anomalous pulmonary venous return.
